fields.Text: The case-study mapping yields six tables: {{c1::EMPLOYEE, DEPARTMENT, DEPT_LOCATIONS, PROJECT, WORKS_ON and DEPENDENT}}.

fields.Front: Case study mapping: schema of EMPLOYEE (with foreign keys)?
fields.Back: EMPLOYEE(SSN, Fname, Minit, Lname, Address, Salary, Sex, Birthdate, SuperSSN FK -> EMPLOYEE, DNumber FK -> DEPARTMENT). SuperSSN comes from SUPERVISES (unary 1:N), DNumber from WORKS FOR.

fields.Front: Case study mapping: schema of DEPARTMENT, and why does it hold the manager?
fields.Back: DEPARTMENT(DNumber, DName, MgrSSN FK -> EMPLOYEE, MgrStartDate). MANAGES is 1:1 and DEPARTMENT has total participation (every department has a manager), so the FK and StartDate go there (Step 3).

fields.Front: Case study mapping: schema of DEPT_LOCATIONS and its primary key?
fields.Back: DEPT_LOCATIONS(DNumber FK, Location); PK (DNumber, Location) (Step 6, multi-valued Locations).

fields.Front: Case study mapping: schema of PROJECT?
fields.Back: PROJECT(PNumber, PName, PLocation, DNumber FK -> DEPARTMENT) (Step 4, CONTROLS 1:N).

fields.Text: WORKS_ON(ESSN, PNumber, Hours) has primary key {{c1::(ESSN, PNumber)}}; both are foreign keys (Step {{c2::5}}, M:N).

fields.Front: Case study mapping: schema of DEPENDENT and its primary key?
fields.Back: DEPENDENT(ESSN FK -> EMPLOYEE, DependentName, Sex, Birthdate, Relationship); PK (ESSN, DependentName) (Step 2, weak entity).

fields.Front: Case study mapping: how is the unary SUPERVISES relationship mapped?
fields.Back: As a foreign key SuperSSN in EMPLOYEE that references EMPLOYEE's own primary key SSN; NULL for the top boss.

fields.Front: Case study mapping: why can two dependents both be named Alice?
fields.Back: Because DEPENDENT's key is (ESSN, DependentName): the same name under different employees is distinct.

fields.Front: What is the objective of the case-study video?
fields.Back: Use the seven rules on ANY ER diagram and convert it into an actual working database in the relational model.

fields.Front: What tool does the instructor use to build the case study database, and why?
fields.Back: Microsoft Access, because it is easy to show quickly on her personal computer.

fields.Front: What happens in Access when you mark a column as the primary key?
fields.Back: It becomes a Required field: the key must always be entered.

fields.Text: Do not leave a new table named {{c1::Table1}}; save it with a meaningful name such as Project.

fields.Front: Why is Location left out of the DEPARTMENT table in the case study?
fields.Back: It is multi-valued, so rule 6 says not to make it an attribute of DEPARTMENT; it gets its own table DEPT_LOCATIONS keyed by (DNumber, Location).

fields.Text: A foreign key column must have the {{c1::same data type}} as the key it references: if DNumber is a Number in DEPARTMENT, it must be a Number in DEPT_LOCATIONS.

fields.Front: How do you create a composite primary key in Access?
fields.Back: Highlight all the key columns together (e.g. DNumber and Location, or ESSN and PNumber) and click Primary Key.

fields.Front: What data types does the instructor choose for EMPLOYEE's SSN, Birthdate and Salary?
fields.Back: SSN: Number (or Short Text, since no calculations are done on it); Birthdate: Date; Salary: Currency.

fields.Front: Why is the DEPENDENTS_OF relationship not mapped again in step 4?
fields.Back: It was already handled in step 2: the weak entity DEPENDENT got the owner's SSN as a foreign key that is part of its key.

fields.Front: Which three columns does step 4 add in the case study?
fields.Back: EMPLOYEE gets the department number (works for) and the supervisor's SSN (supervises); PROJECT gets the managing department number (controls).

fields.Front: What does step 3 add in the case study, and to which table?
fields.Back: MgrSSN (foreign key) and MgrStartDate to DEPARTMENT, the side with total participation in MANAGES.

fields.Front: What sample rows does the instructor enter in WORKS_ON?
fields.Back: Employee 1 on project 45 for 120 hours; employee 1 on project 55 for 100 hours; employee 2 on project 55 for 88 hours.

fields.Front: How do you create a relationship in the Access Relationships window?
fields.Back: Database Tools -> Relationships; add the tables; drag the primary key onto the foreign key column; tick Enforce Referential Integrity; click Create.

fields.Front: How does Access display the unary SUPERVISES relationship?
fields.Back: It shows a second copy of EMPLOYEE to draw the line from SSN to SupervisorSSN, but both boxes are really the same table.

fields.Text: In the case study, step {{c1::6}} needed no extra work (DEPT_LOCATIONS was built right after DEPARTMENT) and step {{c2::7}} did not apply (no ternary relationships).

fields.Front: What mistake does the instructor admit in her EMPLOYEE table, and what does the step 1 rule say?
fields.Back: She stored the whole name in one column; the composite attribute should have been split into first-name and last-name columns.
